questions.stem: Ethanol is heated with ethanoic acid in the presence of a sulfuric acid catalyst. A sweet-smelling product forms. What is this product and what type of reaction has occurred?

options.text: Ethane; a combustion reaction
Ethyl ethanoate; an esterification (condensation) reaction
Ethene; an elimination reaction
Diethyl ether; a substitution reaction

questions.explanation: When a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol, an ester and water are produced. This is called esterification: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. The ester ethyl ethanoate has a characteristic sweet, fruity smell. Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst. Note that this is a reversible reaction.

questions.stem: An ester is named 'propyl methanoate'. Which alcohol and carboxylic acid would you need to make it?

options.text: Methanol and propanoic acid
Propan-1-ol and methanoic acid
Propan-1-ol and ethanoic acid
Methanol and methanoic acid

questions.explanation: Ester names have two parts: the first part comes from the alcohol and the second from the carboxylic acid. 'Propyl' comes from propan-1-ol (a 3-carbon alcohol), and 'methanoate' comes from methanoic acid (HCOOH, a 1-carbon acid). So propyl methanoate = propan-1-ol + methanoic acid.

questions.stem: Many esters have fruity smells and are used as flavourings in food. Pentyl ethanoate smells like bananas. Why are esters suitable for use as food flavourings rather than, say, carboxylic acids?

options.text: Esters are more nutritious than carboxylic acids
Esters have pleasant fruity aromas, while carboxylic acids have sharp, vinegar-like smells and sour tastes
Carboxylic acids are poisonous but esters are not
Esters dissolve better in water than carboxylic acids

questions.explanation: Esters typically have pleasant, sweet, fruity smells that mimic natural fruit aromas (banana, pear, pineapple, etc.). Carboxylic acids, by contrast, tend to have sharp, pungent smells — ethanoic acid smells of vinegar, and butanoic acid smells of rancid butter. The ester functional group (-COO-) gives these compounds their characteristic pleasant aromas.

questions.stem: In the laboratory preparation of an ester, a student mixes ethanol and ethanoic acid but forgets to add the sulfuric acid catalyst. What will happen?

options.text: No ester will form at all under any conditions
The reaction will still occur but extremely slowly because the catalyst lowers the activation energy
An explosion will occur
The reaction will proceed at exactly the same rate

questions.explanation: Esterification can occur without a catalyst, but it is extremely slow at room temperature. Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst, lowering the activation energy and significantly speeding up the reaction. The mixture is also heated in a water bath to further increase the rate. Without the catalyst, the yield of ester would be negligible in a typical lab session.

questions.stem: Esters are used as solvents in nail varnish remover and as plasticisers in plastics. Why are esters useful as solvents?

options.text: They are ionic compounds that dissolve everything
They are volatile liquids that can dissolve organic substances like nail varnish, and they evaporate easily
They are the only liquids that exist at room temperature
They react chemically with the nail varnish to break it down

questions.explanation: Esters are organic compounds that are good at dissolving other organic substances (like the polymers in nail varnish) because of the principle 'like dissolves like'. They are volatile (evaporate easily) due to relatively weak intermolecular forces, which means they evaporate from the nails after dissolving the polish. They are also less toxic than many alternative solvents.
